headline: Rhode Island confirms third Powassan case of 2026
dek: A Washington County resident in his 60s developed symptoms in late August, the state health department said. It is Rhode Island’s 11th reported case since 2016.
body: Rhode Island health officials have confirmed the state’s third case of Powassan virus this year, in a Washington County man in his 60s. The Rhode Island Department of Health said he began experiencing symptoms in late August.

The case brings Rhode Island’s total to 11 since the disease was first reported in the state in 2016. Powassan is a tick-borne infection found mainly in the Northeast, the Great Lakes region and eastern Canada, according to RIDOH.

The department says the illness is rare but can become severe, sometimes affecting the brain and its surrounding membranes. There is no vaccine or specific treatment, making prevention of tick bites the principal protection.

RIDOH advises people outdoors to avoid brush and tall grass, use an EPA-approved repellent, check themselves and pets after returning indoors, and remove attached ticks promptly with tweezers. The department reported 76 U.S. cases in 2025, including 27 in New England.
author: NorthEast News Desk
